observations: body L1-L2, notes_left L9: with 3′ for the Sun at 104ᵖ, Venus at 16ᵖ would have 3′ × 104 : 16 = 19½′, about a third of a part, as Jābir says in note 1 («circiter tertiam partis»).
body L9, L12, L26: the dashes before «Quo» and «Schiaparelli» measure 10.2 and 9.8 pt; a speck over the e of «confidebat» (L12) is not transcribed.

body L13-L14: a heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition; «al–Battānī» has a long dash (5.4 pt), and «120–21» is divided at its dash, which is printed at the end of L13 and again at the beginning of L14 (5.4 pt each).

body L15-L17: the table stands at the places measured on the print; the distances are al-Battānī's of p. 120-121 (S03), the apogee of the Moon, of Mercury and of Venus equal to the perigee of Mercury, of Venus and of the Sun. Recomputed, arcsin(1/64ᵖ 10′) = 53′ 34.6″, arcsin(1/166) = 20′ 42.6″, arcsin(1/1070) = 3′ 12.8″: the table has 53′ 34″, 20′ 42″ and 3′ 13″.

body L20-L26: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the arc AB of the orbit of the Sun (radius 80.8 pt), drawn whole though it prints faint at the right of C, the epicycle CD about I (radius 24.7 pt), which touches it inside at C (their centres 55.8 pt apart, against 56.1 for contact), and the line from C through I and D to T; the bold italic letters stand where they are printed. As drawn, IC : IT is 24.7 : 57.1 = 0.43, not the 0,375 of L22, and T stands 1.3 pt from the centre of the arc.

body L22-L24: with IC = 0,375 IT, TC = IT + IC = 1,375 IT and TD = IT − IC = 0,625 IT (Ptolemy's epicycle of Mercury, 22ᵖ 30′ of 60ᵖ). But 3′ × 1,375 : 0,625 = 3′ × 2,2 = 6′,6 (6′ 36″), not the printed 6′,52; with Ptolemy's 2′ 51″ for the Sun it would be 6′ 16″.
body L27: the dash after «d)» measures 9.4 pt, the hyphen of «15-26» 3.6 pt.

body L29-L32: «ψ» is printed with a straight stem. Formula (α) is al-Battānī's rule of p. 78, L15-L20: the sine and the cosine of the anomaly multiplied by the radius of the epicycle, 5ᵖ 15′, and divided by R; 60ᵖ added to the second; the root of the sum of the squares. 60ᵖ sin 5° 1′ = 5ᵖ 14′ 57″, the radius of the epicycle as «sinus maximae aequationis centri». The dash of «al–Battānī» (L30) measures 5.3 pt.
notes_left L1-L2, L4: the hyphen at the end of «Vene-» prints short and the bracket after «rem» is broken; the m of «summa» is broken.
notes_right L7: a blot over the t of «centrum» is not transcribed.
